notes.decision: Translated as 'the Indweller' tentatively. The lexeme is obscure and resists confident parsing. The overlines on ⲕ̄ may indicate a syllabic abbreviation. Possible analyses: (a) ⲡ-ⲉⲧ-ⲕⲏ-ⲛ 'that which is laid up / the deposit'; (b) ⲡ-ⲛⲏⲧⲕ̄-ⲛ 'the firmly-set one' from ⲧⲱⲕ 'stand fast'; (c) some Manichaean technical title not in our glossary. The text identifies ⲡⲛⲧⲕ̄ⲛ with ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣⲡⲉ 'the New Man' and gives it an icon (line 4). 'Indweller' captures the sense of 'that which exists/dwells in her' (ⲉⲧⲱⲟⲡ ⲛϩⲏⲧⲥ). Flagged for review.
Translated 'blazes a path' / 'sets a way.' Compound: ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲟⲩ- ('a') + ϫⲁⲩ-ⲙⲁⲓⲧ ('way-setting'). Cf. accumulated ⲣⲉϩⲭⲁⲩⲙⲁⲓⲧ 'guide / path-setter' — same root structure.

Translated 'from every life' tentatively. Possibly reduplicated ⲱⲛϩ̄-ⲱⲛϩ̄ 'every-life' or related to ⲍⲱⲱⲛ 'living thing.' The Living Member is redeemed out of all manifestations of life. Awaits parallels.

Translated 'she habitually releases' (lines 13, 14). Likely ϣⲁⲥ-ⲃⲱⲗ habitual + assimilated form, paralleling the cosmologically-significant ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'release' (in glossary). Antithetical pair-partner with ⲱⲁⲥⲱⲛϩ̄ 'she habitually lives' (line 19): in the somatic/psychic registers the soul releases what is not hers; in the pneumatic register she lives and joins. Etymology not certain; could alternatively read 'casts off / strips off.'

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲱⲥ ⲉⲙ ⲡⲉ / ⲛⲱⲥ ⲉⲛ ⲛⲉ
notes.decision: Lycopolitan negative construction with ⲉⲙ/ⲉⲛ for Sah. ⲁⲛ. Translates 'is/are not hers' — possessive ⲡⲱⲥ/ⲛⲱⲥ '(thing) of her / (things) of her' + negation.
The terminal letter ⲉ is marked '(?)' by the editor as uncertain. Preserved in coptic field. Likely the start of relative ⲉⲧⲉ continuing into line 16 (ⲉ-ⲧⲉⲥ-... 'which her-...').
Translated 'discord' / 'division.' Likely Lyc. nominal form of ⲡⲱⲣⲭ/ⲡⲱⲣϫ 'separate, divide' (cf. ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). In the vice-catalogue with ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'envy.'
Lyc. ⲥⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ = Sah. ⲥⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄ 'join, mingle, blend.' Used here of the soul joining inward with patience and faith — the positive incorporation in the pneumatic register.

Translated 'the hour of life.' This is the alternate name (ϫⲉ ...) of the Virgin of Light who is the robe of the New Man. ⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ = Greek ὥρα 'hour, moment' (or = ⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ 'hour'); ⲡⲱⲛϩ̄ 'the life.' She is described as both first and last (line 24) — eschatological-soteriological self-identification.

Treated as the Coptic numeral ⲣⲓⲉ (ⲣ=100, ⲓ=10, ⲉ=5) = 115, the chapter number. The standalone position on a line and the structural following of a chapter-opening narrative ('Once again it happened...' on line 31) supports this reading. The kephalaion's title spans lines 26-30.

Translated 'shall shine forth.' Read as future ⲛⲁ- + verb ⲣⲓⲉ/ⲡⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate' (cf. ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' in glossary; ⲡⲓⲉ 'to shine forth'). The catechumen asks whether rest manifests/shines forth for the deceased. Alternative readings (ⲣⲓⲉ as 'manner' or as a noun) less probable in this syntactic position.
Translated 'a catechumen.' The ⲁⲩ- prefix is Lyc. variant of indefinite article ⲟⲩ-, regular in this dialect. Standard catechumen-introduces-question scenario in the Kephalaia.
